Class FightLearnSession

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.client.Trainer
dev.swordai.client.FightLearnSession
All Implemented Interfaces:
AgentSession
final class FightLearnSession extends Trainer
/swordai fight that the network also learns from: it plays the user's own character against another player, in whatever world or server the user is in, and every fight is gathered, scored with the rewards of the stage it is in, and learned from. What it sees and presses is exactly what FightSession sees and presses.

There is no arena here and no server to ask who hit whom, so everything the rewards need is taken from what this client can see: a flinch tells who was hit, the game client's own reading of its swing tells what kind of hit it was, and the health bars tell the damage. That is a tick or more late and less exact than in training, which is the price of learning from a real fight.

These fights never count towards passing a stage. And the fight does not wait while the network learns from a batch: a copy of it plays on meanwhile (see Trainer.playsOnWhileLearning()).

    • hitsDealtAsShown

      int hitsDealtAsShown(dev.swordai.core.env.StepFacts facts)
      On someone else's server the opponent is seen to flinch a round trip after the swing: four or five ticks at 200 ms. In the arena the network is told of its hit on the tick after the swing, and everything it does next hangs on that: it lets go of W, and it waits for its weapon. Left to wait for the flinch here, it takes every swing for a miss for those ticks and does what it does after a miss, which is to swing again at once (0.13.2, 190 ms: six to seven swings in ten made before the weapon was 60% back, against one in ten in training).

      So here it is told when its own game sent the attack: the swing had the opponent under the crosshair and in reach as its game saw it. That is the same moment it is told in training, and as good as the same thing there. What a hit is worth is still counted from the flinch.

      Overrides:
      hitsDealtAsShown in class Trainer

    • actorNeedsExplained

      float actorNeedsExplained()
      Description copied from class: Trainer
      The least share of a batch's returns the critic has to explain for the actor to learn from that batch. Nothing is asked in the arena. Against people it is: those fights are few, short and unlike anything the critic was trained on, and when it has no idea what a fight was worth, what the actor would learn from it is noise (0.13.2, fights on a server: the critic explained less than nothing of four batches in a row, and the actor was moved by each of them several times as far as a training update moves it).
      Overrides:
      actorNeedsExplained in class Trainer
